exercise: Multinomial Naive Bayes with Bigram Language Model Sentiment Classification

marking_grid.criteria: Correct base formula: P(class|text) = P(class) * \prod P(word|class).
Correct formula incorporating condition on previous word: P(class|text) = P(class) * \prod P(word_i | word_{i-1}, class).
Correct lowercase, punctuation removal, lemmatization, and addition of <s> and </s> tokens for all 4 training sentences.

marking_grid.item: Part 2b: Laplace Smoothing Equation & Vocabulary Size
marking_grid.criteria: Correct smoothing equation P(w_i|w_{i-1},c) = (count(w_{i-1},w_i,c) + 1)/(count(w_{i-1},c) + |V|) with exact vocabulary size |V| = 10.
P(pos) = 0.5, P(neg) = 0.5. Detailed bigram probability calculations showing P(pos|s1) ≈ 0.000174, P(neg|s1) ≈ 0.000027, correctly predicting Positive.

marking_grid.item: Part 3: Reflection on Lemmatization and n-gram Sparsity
marking_grid.criteria: Clear justification of how lemmatization reduces vocabulary sparsity in small datasets and why 4-grams would degrade due to extreme sparsity.

sample_submissions.text:
Training sentences after preprocessing:
Pos 1: <s> like movie good act </s>
Pos 2: <s> like act real good </s>
Neg 1: <s> real bad bad act </s>
Neg 2: <s> play bad real bad hate movie </s>
Vocabulary (10 tokens): ['</s>', '<s>', 'act', 'bad', 'good', 'hate', 'like', 'movie', 'play', 'real'], |V| = 10.
For Test Sentence 1 '<s> like act bad </s>':
P(Positive) = 2/4 = 0.5, P(Negative) = 2/4 = 0.5.
P(like|<s>, Pos) = (2+1)/(2+10) = 3/12 = 0.25
P(act|like, Pos) = (1+1)/(2+10) = 2/12 = 0.1667
P(bad|act, Pos) = (0+1)/(2+10) = 1/12 = 0.0833
P(</s>|bad, Pos) = (0+1)/(0+10) = 1/10 = 0.1000
P(Pos|s1) = 0.5 * 0.25 * 0.1667 * 0.0833 * 0.1 = 1.736e-4
P(Neg|s1) = 0.5 * (1/12) * (1/10) * (1/11) * (1/14) = 2.705e-5
Since 1.736e-4 > 2.705e-5, Predicted Class is Positive.
sample_submissions.feedback: Perfect score (7.5/7.5). Complete preprocessing with boundary tokens, exact Laplace smoothing fractions, step-by-step prior and bigram products, and justified decision.

exercise: CKY Parsing: CNF Conversion and Dynamic Programming Table

marking_grid.item: Step 1: CNF Elimination of Unit Productions
marking_grid.criteria: Replaces unit production NP -> N with direct terminal productions NP -> 'chat' | 'chien' | 'fille' | etc.

marking_grid.item: Step 2: CNF Rules with > 2 RHS symbols
marking_grid.criteria: Introduces new non-terminals X1 -> Det N (NP -> X1 PP) and X2 -> V NP (VP -> X2 PP).

marking_grid.item: Step 3: CKY Dynamic Programming Table Fill
marking_grid.criteria: Correct upper-triangular matrix entries for 'le chat voit un chien dans le parc' with correct S symbol at cell [0, 8].

sample_submissions.text:
1. Convert Unit Productions: NP -> N is replaced by NP -> 'chat' | 'chien' | 'fille' | 'garçon' | 'maison' | 'parc'.
2. Convert > 2 RHS symbols: NP -> Det N PP becomes NP -> X1 PP and X1 -> Det N. VP -> V NP PP becomes VP -> X2 PP and X2 -> V NP.
3. Final CNF rules: S -> NP VP | S PP; NP -> Det N | X1 PP | terminals; VP -> V NP | V PP | X2 PP; PP -> P NP.
4. Cell [0, 8] correctly contains S deriving the complete 8-word sentence.
sample_submissions.feedback: Full marks (4.5/4.5). Flawless CNF transformation preserving all conventions and exact dynamic programming table derivation.
